summary: Cora Vreede-de Stuers studied at the University of Paris (Ph.D. 1957), where she also worked as a librarian (1932–1936). She served as head librarian at the University of Indonesia and later taught cultural anthropology at the University of Amsterdam.

Corinna May Lhoir works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She is a doctoral student at Ghent University and a doctoral researcher and lecturer at the University of Hamburg, where she also held an administrative assistance post attested 2021–2026.

Corneille Jest was a Tibetology and history and archaeology scholar who studied at Paris Descartes University and under André Leroi-Gourhan. From circa 1957 to 1995, he held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique.

Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar Cornelis Jan Kuiken completed his MA under Jaap den Hollander and his PhD in 2002 at the University of Groningen under doctoral supervisors Timothy Hugh Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele was a religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who studied at Amsterdam and the Remonstrant Seminary. He served as a Remonstrant pastor, seminary professor, and Professor of the History of Religions at Leiden University (1877–1901).

id: P:Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden
summary: Cornelius Wilhelmus Josef van der Linden was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. in 1954 from Utrecht University under the supervision of Jan Gonda.
Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli. He served as a professor at Sapienza University of Rome, attested in 1971.

Cortland Dahl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche and received mentorship from Sarah Harding, Anne Helm, and Erik Pema Kunsang.

Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar Courtney Bruntz served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015). She later joined the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research as Core Faculty, Professor, and Director of Assessment and Accreditation.

Craig Jamieson is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who served as a fellow of Queens' College and held posts at the University of Cambridge, including curator for the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2012).
Craig Preston is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981) and Joe Bransford Wilson.

Indologist Cristina Pecchia earned her PhD at Sapienza University of Rome, studying under Raniero Gnoli, Raffaele Torella, and Corrado Pensa, and later studied under Ernst Steinkellner. Around 2006, she held posts at Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, earned her doctorate under Jacques May. She served as a professor at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1999–2015) and the University of Lausanne (~2000–2012).

Indologist Csaba Dezső earned master's degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and completed his PhD at the University of Oxford (1998–2004) under Alexis Sanderson. Around 2001, he served as an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

Indologist Csaba Kiss earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2019–2024) and as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University.

Cuilan Liu works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She held posts as Assistant Professor of Buddhist Studies at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and at the University of Munich (attested 2018).
Culadasa was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied under traditional teacher Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu and served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
Cunda studied under Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Amaro.

Cuong T. Mai, a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, earned an MA from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD from Indiana University Bloomington under John R. McRae. He served as Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Vermont.
